title: A Counterexample To The TF-cone Conjecture
summary: The TF-cone conjecture of Asai and Iyama predicts that the TF equivalence class of an integral $g$-vector is the open cone generated by the canonical summands of all its positive multiples. We give a counterexample to this conjecture. For the tensor product of the three-arrow Kronecker algebra with the path algebra of $s\to t$, a vector $w$ has a two-dimensional TF equivalence class, whereas every positive integral multiple $mw$ is generically indecomposable.
